column3: The primary goal of TLS is to provide a secure channel between two communicating peers (`rfc8446#section-1`).
column5: The primary goal of TLS is to provide a secure channel between two communicating peers

column3: In TLS, confidentiality means that data sent over the channel after establishment is only visible to the endpoints (`rfc8446#section-1`).
column5: Confidentiality: Data sent over the channel after establishment is only visible to the endpoints.

column3: In TLS, integrity means that data sent over the channel after establishment cannot be modified by attackers without detection (`rfc8446#section-1`).
column5: Integrity: Data sent over the channel after establishment cannot be modified by attackers without detection.

column3: TLS does not hide the length of the data it transmits, though endpoints are able to pad TLS records in order to obscure lengths (`rfc8446#section-1`).
column5: TLS does not hide the length of the data it transmits, though endpoints are able to pad TLS records in order to obscure lengths and improve protection against traffic analysis techniques.

column3: TLS consists of two primary components, the first being a handshake protocol that authenticates the communicating parties, negotiates cryptographic modes and parameters, and establishes shared keying material (`rfc8446#section-1`).
column5: TLS consists of two primary components: - A handshake protocol (Section 4) that authenticates the communicating parties, negotiates cryptographic modes and parameters, and establishes shared keying material.

column3: The second primary component of TLS is a record protocol that uses the parameters established by the handshake protocol to protect traffic between the communicating peers (`rfc8446#section-1`).
column5: A record protocol (Section 5) that uses the parameters established by the handshake protocol to protect traffic between the communicating peers.

column3: In a Kubernetes `EncryptionConfiguration`, the first provider in the list is used to encrypt resources written into the storage (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: The first provider in the list is used to encrypt resources written into the storage.

column3: When reading resources from storage, each provider that matches the stored data attempts in order to decrypt the data (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: When reading resources from storage, each provider that matches the stored data attempts in order to decrypt the data.

column3: If no provider can read the stored data due to a mismatch in format or secret key, an error is returned which prevents clients from accessing that resource (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: If no provider can read the stored data due to a mismatch in format or secret key, an error is returned which prevents clients from accessing that resource.

column3: Only one provider type may be specified per entry of the `providers` array (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: Only one provider type may be specified per entry (identity or aescbc may be provided, but not both in the same item).

column3: Each provider supports multiple keys, the keys are tried in order for decryption, and if the provider is the first provider, the first key is used for encryption (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: Each provider supports multiple keys - the keys are tried in order for decryption, and if the provider is the first provider, the first key is used for encryption.

column3: In the example `EncryptionConfiguration`, the `identity` provider is annotated as plain text, in other words no encryption (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: identity: {} # plain text, in other words NO encryption

column3: If custom resources are added to `EncryptionConfiguration` and the cluster version is 1.26 or newer, any newly created custom resources mentioned in the `EncryptionConfiguration` will be encrypted (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: If custom resources are added to EncryptionConfiguration and the cluster version is 1.26 or newer, any newly created custom resources mentioned in the EncryptionConfiguration will be encrypted.

column3: Any custom resources that existed in etcd prior to that version and configuration will be unencrypted until they are next written to storage (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: Any custom resources that existed in etcd prior to that version and configuration will be unencrypted until they are next written to storage.

column3: The `'*.*'` entry will encrypt all resources, even custom resources that are added after API server start (`k8s-encrypt-data#understanding-the-encryption-at-rest-configuration`).
column5: '*.*' will encrypt all resources, even custom resources that are added after API server start.
